clues.text: Reaching a top speed of 50 mph, this 108-foot-tall coaster sends riders through 5 inversions.
This coaster was engineered by legendary Swiss manufacturer B&M and opened in 1997.
Thrill-seekers can find this inverted coaster operating in the state of Texas.
This attraction holds the distinction of being the very first roller coaster built at a SeaWorld park.
This coaster takes its ferocious name from a legendary apex predator that roams the ocean: a massive species of shark.

evidence.quote: It was the first inverted roller coaster to be built in Texas.
The Great White is an inverted roller coaster at SeaWorld San Antonio, and the first roller coaster to be built at a SeaWorld park.
The ride takes its name from the ''Great White'' shark.
